subject: Logic
title: Propositions and Variables
description: A micro-lesson that makes Propositions and Variables usable.

hook.text: In formal logic, "It is raining" becomes just P. One letter carries the entire statement.

buildup.text: A proposition is any statement that's either true or false. We assign it a variable: P, Q, R, and so on.

discovery.text: Variables let us study argument structure without caring about content. P → Q works for any P and Q.

twist.text: This abstraction is the power move: one formula proves validity for millions of different real-world arguments.

climax.text: By stripping content away, formal logic reveals that structure alone determines validity.

quiz.question: What does a propositional variable like P represent?
options: A statement that is true or false
